status: Complete digital first-edition script; initial bilingual comparison; independent fluent-reader review pending.

panels.action: Plain shaded home workshop courtyard. Tara at left proudly places a small shallow open rectangular cardboard toy cart on a flat wooden test board. Kanu at right leans in to test; Dinu stands behind, watching. Cart has two straight thin axles across its width and four round cardboard disc wheels. Consistent simple props, no text or markings other than plain drawing lines.

caption.or: ତାରାର ଛୋଟ ଖେଳଣା ଗାଡ଼ି ପରୀକ୍ଷା ପାଇଁ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ।
caption.en: Tara’s little toy cart is ready for its first test.

panels.action: Low close view of Kanu gently rolling the cart along the flat test board. It tilts and bobs because the near front wheel's hole is visibly off-centre. Small motion strokes show irregular movement. Tara looks annoyed at the imperfect result. The board is completely flat; do not add rocks, bumps or a crooked axle as alternative causes.

dialogue.speaker: kanu
dialogue.or: ଆରେ, ସମତଳ ପଟାରେ ବି ଗାଡ଼ିଟା ଡେଉଁଛି!
dialogue.en: It’s bouncing even on a flat board!

dialogue.speaker: tara
dialogue.en: It’ll be fine if I smooth the wheel’s edge.

panels.action: Tara has smoothed the cardboard rim with a small sandpaper scrap now resting on the table. The cart still bobs. Dinu invites them to look closer with an open hand, not taking over the cart. Kanu slows his test and crouches to wheel height. Keep Tara left, Kanu right, Dinu behind.

caption.or: ଧାର ମସୃଣ ହେଲା। ଗାଡ଼ି କିନ୍ତୁ ସେମିତି।
caption.en: The edge is smooth. The cart still wobbles.

dialogue.speaker: tara
dialogue.en: Why is it still doing that?

dialogue.speaker: dinu
dialogue.or: ଟିକେ ଧୀରେ ଚଲାଅ। ଏଇ ଚକଟାକୁ ଦେଖ।
dialogue.en: Roll it slowly. Watch this wheel.

panels.action: The discovery: close-up of ONE detached round cardboard wheel held upright by Tara at its rim, facing viewer. Its axle hole is unmistakably off-centre, halfway between centre and upper-right rim. A small pencil cross marks the actual centre, clearly separate from that hole. Kanu points to the wrong hole; both children's faces show recognition at edges of panel. No text or labels. This is the key visual evidence; keep disc large, truly round and hole offset, not centred.

dialogue.speaker: kanu
dialogue.en: This wheel keeps going up and down!

dialogue.speaker: tara
dialogue.en: Oh! The hole isn’t in the middle!

panels.action: Repair on the worktable. A NEW cardboard wheel lies flat with a small cross at its exact centre. Tara has marked it with ruler and pencil and now watches. Dinu alone uses a short hand-held awl vertically at the centre over a thick scrap wooden block, his fingers well to the side. Kanu watches. The OLD off-centre wheel lies separately to the left for comparison; only two detached wheels in view. Children do not hold sharp tools. The partly disassembled cart is in background. No power tool.

dialogue.speaker: tara
dialogue.or: ନୂଆ ଚକର ମଝିଟା ଆଗେ ଚିହ୍ନ ଦେବା।
dialogue.en: Let’s mark the middle of a new wheel first.

panels.action: Cart now runs level along the SAME flat test board carrying two small wooden blocks. Kanu holds one extra small block, looking hopefully toward Tara, with a modest pile of spare blocks nearby. Tara smiles and raises ONE finger for one at a time. Dinu watches amused in background with hands behind back. All three share the success. No bouncing motion strokes, no off-centre hole on the repaired front wheel.

dialogue.speaker: kanu
dialogue.or: ଏଥର ତ ଭଲ ଚାଲୁଛି। ଆଉ ଗୋଟେ କାଠ ଖଣ୍ଡ ରଖିବା?
dialogue.en: It’s running smoothly now. One more wooden block?

dialogue.speaker: tara
dialogue.or: ଆଗେ ଗୋଟେ! ସବୁ କାଠ ଏକାଥରେ ନୁହେଁ!
dialogue.en: One first! Not the whole pile!

review.sourceText: New Odia script written for this project; English companion compared against each line.
checks: Six stages preserve the same cause: an off-centre axle hole.
The board remains flat and the axle straight, avoiding a competing diagnosis.
Kanu observes; Tara diagnoses; Dinu helps with making the hole.
The original mistaken rim repair remains visible.
Odia and English retain the same relationships, test sequence and gentle last-line joke.
openPoints: Fluent-reader check of conversational ଡେଉଁଛି and natural workshop vocabulary before any print edition.
